title: Any ways to analyze/resolve crashes using AI?
author: MosesSecondofHisName
selftext:
I've got a game in the Play Store now and have been using Firebase Crashlytics to monitor its health. I've gotten some ANRs and crashes, but when I run them through Codex, it can't confidently find solutions, in part because it only has access to the game files, not all the mediating factors that are involved in deloyment.

Has anyone found a way to get more accurate crash info? Alternatively, is there a certain amount or type of crashing that is acceptable? In typing this, I just realized that I've played plenty of even AAA games that crash under the right conditions. Maybe eliminating crashes is always a bit of an unwinnable game of whack a mole?

comments.author: Rsouss
comments.body: Enter your game, identify the error, and explain it to the codex with as much information as possible: when, where, and how. Send this information to Sol. At most.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I generally use the biggest models available (Sol, Fable) for this kind of work. Give access to the codebase, plus the crash data, and ask for theories about what caused the crashes. 

I don’t know what you mean by “it only has access to the game files”.

replies.author: MosesSecondofHisName
replies.body:
Sorry, by game files, I meant codebase.

What do you use for crash data? So far, I've just copy and pasted the brief crash description from Crashlytics. Is there somewhere I could find a more in-depth crash report?

comments.author: TechgeekOne
comments.body: You'll need dumps and logs from the crash. Many operating systems collect that info somewhere for you, it's just a matter of getting the files. Once you got that info + the code usually it's pretty easy to find and resolve.
